# OpenFullPage

> A Chrome extension that captures a whole web page as one image, annotates it and
> saves it. It makes no network requests at all: the extension manifest sets
> `connect-src 'none'`, so Chrome itself refuses to carry any outbound traffic.
> Free, open source under GPL-3.0, no account, no analytics, no build step.

## What it does

- Captures a full web page of any length as a single image, not just the visible area.
- Also captures the visible area only, or one selected element.
- Holds sticky and fixed elements still while scrolling so they do not repeat down the image.
- Waits for lazy loaded images before capturing each screenful.
- Annotates with arrows, lines, boxes, ellipses, a highlighter, text and numbered steps.
- Redacts by resampling the pixels and flattening on export, so the original is not recoverable from the saved file.
- Crops, undoes and redoes.
- Exports as PNG or JPEG, or copies to the clipboard.

## What makes it different

Every extension in this category claims to respect privacy. This one is built so the
claim can be checked rather than believed:

1. No network access. `connect-src 'none'` in the manifest blocks fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and beacons at the browser level.
2. No remote code. No eval, no new Function, no update server, no remotely fetched configuration.
3. No dependencies and no build step. The installed package is byte identical to the public source, and the build proves it by diffing them.
4. No broad permissions at install: only activeTab, scripting and storage. Downloads is requested on first save. Wider site access is optional, off by default and revocable.
5. No synced storage, so settings never leave the machine that made them.

Each of the five is checked on every commit and fails the build if broken.

## Permissions in detail

- `activeTab` (at install): read the current page, and only after the toolbar button is clicked on it.
- `scripting` (at install): run the scrolling and measuring code, only where activeTab already allows it.
- `storage` (at install): remember settings locally. Never `chrome.storage.sync`.
- `downloads` (requested on first save): write the image to the downloads folder. Declining still allows a manual right click and save.
- `webNavigation` plus site access (optional, off by default): capture the full contents of cross-origin iframes instead of only what is on screen.

Even with all of these granted, the content security policy still blocks every
outbound request. The permissions allow reading a page; none of them allows sending
what was read anywhere.

## Requirements

Chrome 116 or newer on Windows, macOS, Linux or ChromeOS. Manifest V3. No account,
no sign in, no configuration required.
